summary: The prepared base already resolved the original zero-reserved-token completion overflow but still failed reserved-token accounting. The exact candidate preserves feasible automatic truncation, correctly accounts for reserved tokens, and rejects the impossible reserved>context configuration without mutating the request. Its focused suite passed, and an independent 49,152-case grid found no invalid acceptance or unexpected rejection.

tests.what_was_measured: The original 6+8>10 case was already auto-truncated to 6+4 on the prepared base. The inherited reserved-token case failed the invariant with prompt=10, reserved=3, completion=0, total=13 at context=10.
Candidate regression and adjacent compatibility coverage: 13 tests and 11 subtests passed.
Original total overflow, prompt overflow, feasible reserved budgets, reserved==context, reserved>context rejection, and disabled-auto-truncate compatibility all behaved as required.

tests.command: Independent exhaustive TokenizerManager grid: context=1..12; prompt, completion, reserved=0..15 (exact candidate)
tests.what_was_measured: 49,152 combinations: 23,040 accepted, 26,112 rejected, zero accepted totals above context, and zero rejections where reserved<=context.
The candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X was visible, but no compatible EAGLE speculative draft model/weights were available. The qualified tiny Llama fixture cannot exercise nonzero reserved tokens, so no unrelated GPU smoke was used as proof.

remaining_limitations: Nonzero reserved-token behavior was validated directly at TokenizerManager rather than end-to-end with an EAGLE model because compatible draft weights were unavailable.
The deterministic tiny Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only and cannot qualify the EAGLE-specific reserved-token path.
No native source changed, so native rebuild and compiler/ISA validation were not applicable.
Independent GPU numerical comparison is not applicable to deterministic request-length control flow.
